analysis.title: UBS House View - Daily US: Semis stumble. Time to reboot expectations?
key_insights: UBS CIO sees the chip sell-off as a reset in expectations, not a deterioration in the underlying AI investment cycle. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is down around 8% over five sessions and the Kospi is down over 12% since the start of October.

Drivers of the sell-off named in the note: durability of AI spending, competition from China's rising memory maker, higher-for-longer rates, the debate over OpenAI's reported revenue trajectory, and a Broadcom CEO warning that financing the AI buildout could become a bigger constraint than component shortages.

The OpenAI revenue shortfall reports were later clarified as mostly differing accounting treatments, not a meaningful change in demand. UBS treats hyperscaler cloud growth as one of the clearest real-time indicators of AI monetization.
ASML reported stronger-than-expected earnings on Wednesday and raised the low end of its 2026 revenue forecast for a third consecutive quarter.
Positive EPS guidance among S&P 500 companies is tracking at a five-year high. UBS expects S&P 500 earnings growth of around 28% in the coming reporting season, with semiconductors a key contributor.

UBS expects the Q3 reporting season to matter more for sentiment than headlines on competition or financing constraints. Earnings growth is moderating, but UBS says direction depends on the profit outlook and revisions more than on the pace of deceleration.

UBS says the backdrop differs from the 2022 tech correction: base case is only modest Fed tightening, semiconductor valuations are below long-term averages, and long debt maturities limit the impact of higher rates on earnings.

UBS suggests investors may consider adding exposure to the 'Magnificent 6'. Within the AI supply chain it favors semi-cap and robotics equipment, then foundry/OSAT and compute beneficiaries. Memory ranks lower despite optically attractive valuations because of medium-term supply concerns and added capacity risk.

NY Fed President Williams said one more rate hike may be appropriate this year but sees no reason for a further hike in 2027. He expects inflation to move closer to 2% next year as tariff and energy effects fade, and is still assessing AI-infrastructure-linked price pressure. He called the labor market balanced and the economy not overheating.

Investors expect a Fed hike in December and two more in 2027, while a number of other Fed officials believe more than one additional hike is needed. Wednesday's CPI report is the last before the 27-28 October FOMC meeting.

UBS base case is that the Fed waits until December to hike rather than moving in October, citing softer employment data, slower wage growth and encouraging underlying inflation trends. It expects a measured tightening cycle.

MAS surprised markets by leaving Singapore dollar policy settings unchanged, pausing a tightening cycle that included increases in April and July. The SGD weakened against the USD. MAS narrowed its 2026 core inflation forecast to 1.5-2.0% and kept 1.5-2.5% for 2027.
UBS expects USDSGD to fall gradually to 1.25 over 12 months from just above 1.28 now, and calls SGD an attractive diversification currency for USD-based investors.

UBS favors diversified, active exposure across the AI value chain, balancing semiconductors with platform companies and defensive technology segments that benefit from software, cloud and productivity adoption.

tension_points.bull_case: UBS sees a reset in expectations, not a break in the AI investment cycle: cloud growth is accelerating, S&P 500 positive EPS guidance is at a five-year high, ASML raised its 2026 revenue forecast floor a third straight quarter, and semiconductor valuations are below long-term averages.
tension_points.bear_case: The sell-off reflects doubts about AI spending durability, competition from China's memory maker, higher-for-longer rates, OpenAI revenue concerns and the Broadcom CEO's warning that financing could become the binding constraint.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Q3 earnings and revisions that fail to show AI spending translating into sustainable earnings growth.

theme_stances.key_argument: The sell-off is a recalibration of expectations rather than a fundamental break in the AI investment story.
theme_stances.evidence: more of a reset in expectations than a deterioration

theme_stances.key_argument: The Fed can remain patient and wait until December to raise rates again rather than tightening in October.
theme_stances.evidence: policymakers can wait until December before raising rates again
